correctness.rationale: The language has three disjoint sorts R,C,S and ternary predicate L(r,c,s), without named constants or function symbols. Each order n has n elements in each sort. Sentences asserting at least j distinct rows distinguish n<4. Orders 1–3 each have unique isotopy class, hence unique three-sorted structure up to isomorphism. For arbitrary n≥4, the one-element atomic extension patterns above tuples of length at most three depend only on the sort/equality/Latin-incidence pattern: three same sort, two plus one, and one of each exhaust the cases; Latin row/column/symbol uniqueness plus at least four elements realize every consistent extension pattern. The same back-and-forth successor pattern thus yields Duplicator strategy for four EF rounds in any two such structures. A 2x2 rectangle with exactly three symbols has a rank-five formula (four nested row/column quantifiers followed by two sibling symbol quantifiers) true in the Z4 table but false in V4, proving the threshold sharp for this algebraic pair. Fresh independent atomic-type successor calculations for Z4,V4,Z5 and direct rectangle checks corroborate; arbitrary order follows from the structural one-point extension proof, not samples.
